body:
Two things are now on the table that the original account lacked: the objection's reordering (the avoidance as possibly load-bearing, the record as possibly optional) and the rival's discriminating probe plus a third reading (arguments as standing-negotiation, with the absence of a record doing work rather than marking a failure). The instruction for this node is to decide, so here are the decisions and the grounds where they matter.

I accept the objection's order-of-operations point and reject the account's implied sequence. The decisive ground is the objection's sharpest observation: a weekly check-in is more of the thing that already failed, addressed to the person who withdrew from it. Both the record and the check-in presuppose a cooperative conversation that the avoidance shows is currently not happening; instituting apparatus first puts the apparatus before its own precondition. So: conversation first, record conditional.

I adopt the rival's probe as the cheapest discriminating instrument, with two modifications. First, ask about the last two or three disputes, not one, because a single remembered disagreement may be unrepresentative. Second, code the answers by axis: what words were said (memorial, supports the account), what the task covered or whether it recurred (scope, supports the rival's second reading), what ought to count now given the schedule change (normative, supports the objection's emphasis), or who is at fault (blame-routing, weak support for the standing reading). The rival is right that the probe measures present reports rather than past events, and that is sufficient: the choice here is between remedies, and remedies should match the axis people actually fight on, not the axis that truly failed.

One correction to the objection. Its commitments state that disputes continuing after a record-plus-definitions trial would count against the objection. On the objection's own logic that is backwards: continued disputes is exactly what it predicts, since records do not settle normative questions. The consistent mapping is: disputes ending counts against the objection's ranking; disputes persisting weakens the account's memorial reading; disputes relocating onto the record itself (arguing about who wrote what) supports the rival's third reading. Stating that mapping in advance is also the answer to the objection's fairest complaint, that the account's test could be read as supporting it either way — though note the account did pre-commit to a falsifier and declared a quiet week uninformative, so the test was better specified than the objection allows. What was genuinely missing are two things. First, the account's remedy sentence bundled two interventions: a record, which addresses memory, and concrete definitions of done, which address norms. The objection's distinction shows the definitions do the normative work, so even a quieting outcome could not be cleanly credited to the record — and the practical consequence is that the definitional practice can be kept while the ledger is skipped, which lands close to the rival's scope-aloud proposal. Second, two outcome variables must be tracked separately: recurrence of chore disputes, and the avoidant friend's participation. The account watched only the first; the objection's ranking is really about the second. A quiet record with a still-absent friend vindicates the objection; a still-noisy record with a re-engaged friend supports the account's sequencing after all.

A smaller correction to the rival: it says the account treats the one-to-one approach as clearly correct. It does not; the account flags that move as its most contestable part. The real disagreement is about sequencing confidence and framing, not about whether the risk exists, and I take the rival's substantive point anyway: the conversation should ask for their view of the group's conversations, not why they withdraw.

One constraint nobody has stated plainly: the person asking is one of the three flatmates. There is no neutral observer in this material. Every probe, note, and check-in will be heard partly as a move in the dispute — the rival gestures at this and the account flags surveillance risk, but all three write as if a trial could be run from outside. It cannot. Consequence: the probe must be presented as the asker's own attempt to understand, and the asker should run it on themselves first — privately write down what they think the last few agreements were, then in each one-to-one offer that before asking ('here is what I thought we had agreed; what did you think?'), which lowers the interrogation register the rival worried about.

The sequence I end with: self-probe first, no apparatus; then two one-to-ones in the reframed form with the probe embedded and answers coded by axis; then match the remedy to what returns. Words-said clustering makes a minimal shared note proportionate. Scope or recurrence clustering calls for stating scope aloud at the moment of agreement, no ledger required. Normative clustering calls for the thing neither predecessor named: an explicit conversation about what counts as fair under changing schedules, because if the fights are normative the remedy is normative rather than documentary. Blame-routing or no clustering weakens the memory reading and makes the conversation pattern itself the next subject — the objection's naming-the-avoidance applied to the group. Whatever is tried, track both outcome variables, treat a quiet week as uninformative, and treat the avoidant friend's response to any record as primary data about its social cost.

Deliberately left open: whether the household wants any system at all, which is the first question inside the one-to-ones; the standing-negotiation reading, live but evidence-free; the onset of the avoidance relative to the schedule changes; the chore inventory and load symmetry. Nothing here settles those; the probes are how the household's own answers start doing the work our conjectures have been doing.
commitments:
Taking this up involves, first, a claim I am prepared to lose: conversation should precede apparatus. The grounds are the objection's, and I can already see the exception — if the avoidant friend is avoiding talk specifically rather than the subject of talk, a written channel may suit them better than a conversation, which would invert my ordering for that one person. A single finding could reverse the sequencing, and I hold it loosely enough to let it.

Second, a correction offered as a friendly amendment, itself revisable: I read the objection's stated test-direction (continued disputes counting against it) as inconsistent with its own logic and restated it. If there is a coherent reading of that wording I have missed, the amendment should be re-amended; what I am committed to is not the correction but the practice of stating outcome-interpretations before outcomes are known.

Third, an application proposal with its limitation stated in advance: the coding axes (words said, scope, recurrence, normative-ought, blame-routing) are my construct. Real disputes may cluster on things the scheme cannot see — tone, who raised the topic, whether being asked felt like a demand. If returned answers refuse the coding, that counts against my instrument, not against the household. I also inherit the rival's self-denying condition: non-clustering answers are not to be recruited as evidence for whichever reading I already favor.

Fourth, a dependence exposed rather than hidden: the whole sequence assumes the asker is a fair-enough conductor of it. If the asker is themselves the friction — a possibility nothing in the material excludes — the one-to-one answers will be shaped by that, and every axis inherits the distortion. I cannot correct for this from here; I can only keep it as a standing caveat on all of the above.

Fifth, a small criticism with its grounds, held cheaply: the rival mischaracterized the account as presenting the one-to-one as clearly correct, when the account flagged that move as its most contestable part. If the account somewhere does present it as settled, my correction lapses.

Unresolved and not to be papered over: the chore inventory, failure rate, escalation history, load symmetry, the avoidance's onset, the standing reading's complete lack of current evidence, and whether the household wants any system. My remedy-matching rule presumes the one-to-ones happen; if both friends decline, that refutes no reading, but it leaves avoidance-centrality as the only hypothesis still doing work, which is itself a reportable outcome rather than a procedural failure.

What I propose to take up if this continues: drafting the actual self-probe format, the two one-to-one questions, and the pre-specified outcome mapping with both tracked variables, so a later node can evaluate whatever those conversations return instead of generating further conjecture about people none of us has heard from.
